    Proposition 10.3 in coefficients #

    The source paper (prop:integral-bockstein): "In Lemma 10.2, the map j is zero by (mod-four-mesh-annihilator). Injectivity of Ψ₄ gives i_* = 0."

    In coefficients (RaySys.Sys.IStar): for a cochain z of character χ over 𝒪 = ℤ/4 with d₂z ∈ 2C³, the cochain 2z is d₁ of a cochain. Its reduction z̄ is a cocycle over 𝔽₂; the cocycle Φ₂(2z) = 2Φ₂(z) of A⁽⁴⁾ = 𝒪P is twice the cocycle Φ₂(z̄) of A⁽²⁾ ≅ 𝔽₂P, a coboundary by MeshWalk.exists_hcobdry_twice, and the coefficients of a coboundary are d₁ of coefficients (coef_of_hcobdry). For A this runs in the prime-field model C⁽²⁾ with Θ₂ : 𝔽₂P ≅ A⁽²⁾ (IndSkeleton.tab₂) and the rows of IndSkeleton.prime_cokerSpan. This proves IStarHyp, hence Cor105Hyp (cor105Hyp).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.integralBockstein (k : Type u') [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharP k 2] (A : Type u') [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] [IsNoetherianRing Aᵐᵒᵖ] (hbasic : IsBasicAlgebra A) (hA : IsRepresentationFiniteRight k A) (S : IndSkeleton k A) (b : S.ArrowBases) (v₀ : S.ARVertex) (hF : IsRepresentationFiniteRight k (CatAlg.Alg (S.arMeshData b).F0)ᵐᵒᵖ) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (Wd : ι → MeshWalk.MeshWt S.arTranslationQuiver ℤ) (Rw : ι → (x : ↑S.arTranslationQuiver.nonprojective) × Quiver.Path ↑(S.arTranslationQuiver.tau x) ↑x) (i : ι) :
    0 < (MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).P.deg (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) → ∀ (c : (MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).C2 (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) (ZMod 2)), ((MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).d2L (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) (ZMod 2)) c = 0 → ∃ (δ : (MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).C1 (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) (ZMod 4)), ((MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).d1L (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) (ZMod 4)) δ = 2 • Z4.lift ∘ c ∧ (MeshWalk.SysD (S.arMeshData b) v₀ hF Wd).d1 (MeshWalk.rowWt (MeshWalk.dualWt Wd) (Rw i)) (ZMod 2) (⇑Z4.red ∘ δ) = 0

    Proposition 10.3 (prop:integral-bockstein), as stated: for every basic representation-finite algebra in characteristic two and every positive character χ of the dual weights, the connecting map is surjective — every two-cocycle c over 𝔽₂ of character χ (of A⁽²⁾ ≅ 𝔽₂P) is (dδ)/2 for a one-cochain δ over ℤ/4 whose reduction is a derivation.
